## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `FtpSftp`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `ftp-sftp`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **FtpSftp**.

## Step 2: Creating an FTP service

1. Select **+ Add Artifact** in the canvas or click **+** next to **Entry Points** in the sidebar.
2. In the **Artifacts** panel, select **FTP / SFTP** under **File Integration**.
3. <!-- manual: In the Create FTP Integration form, keep Protocol set to ftp. -->
4. <!-- manual: Fill in the Listener Configuration: -->
5. <!-- manual: Choose an authentication method: -->
6. <!-- manual: Enter the Monitoring Path — the directory on the remote server to poll for new files (e.g., /uploads). Defaults to /. -->
7. Select **Create**. WSO2 Integrator opens the service in the **Service Designer** with the listener pill attached.
8. Select **+ Add File Handler** to define how incoming files are processed.

## Step 3: Creating an FTPS service

1. Select **+ Add Artifact** → **FTP / SFTP** under **File Integration**.
2. In the **Create FTP Integration** form, select **Protocol** → **ftps**.
3. <!-- manual: Fill in the Listener Configuration: -->
4. <!-- manual: Choose an authentication method: -->
5. Select **Advanced Configurations**.
6. <!-- manual: Enter the Monitoring Path and click Create. -->
7. Select **+ Add File Handler** in the Service Designer to define how incoming files are processed.

## Step 4: Creating an SFTP service

1. Select **+ Add Artifact** → **FTP / SFTP** under **File Integration**.
2. In the **Create FTP Integration** form, select **Protocol** → **sftp**.
3. <!-- manual: Fill in the Listener Configuration: -->
4. Select **Certificate-Based Authentication** under **authentication method**. This reveals the **Private Key** and **Username** fields.
5. <!-- manual: Enter the Private Key record. Click Record on the field and supply: If the private key is passphrase-protected, include the passphrase in the record: -->
6. <!-- manual: Enter the Username that matches the configured private key and the Monitoring Path. -->
7. Select **Create**.
8. Select **+ Add File Handler** in the Service Designer.

## Step 5: Reusing an existing listener when creating a service

1. Select **+ Add Artifact** → **FTP / SFTP** under **File Integration** to open the **Create FTP Integration** form.
2. When the integration already has at least one FTP listener, the **Select an existing FTP listener or create a new one** picker at the top of the form defaults to **Use existing**. Sharing a listener is the encouraged flow for the second and subsequent services. (**Create new** should only be used when you want a dedicated listener for this service.).
3. The **Listener Name** field is a dropdown prefilled with the first available listener. Pick a different one if needed. **Protocol**, **Host**, **Port Number**, and the authentication method are locked (they belong to the listener, not to this service) so you can see the settings the new service will inherit but cannot change them here.
4. <!-- manual: Enter the Monitoring Path for the new service (this is service-level, so it stays editable even under Use existing) and click Create. -->
5. The project tree now shows both services under **Entry Points** and the single shared listener under **Listeners**:.

## Step 6: Attaching an additional listener to an existing service

1. <!-- manual: Open the service you want to extend — click the FTP Integration - &lt;path&gt; entry in the project tree. -->
2. In the **Service Designer**, select **Configure** to open the **FTP Integration Configuration** panel. The left-hand nav pane lists the service's current listeners under **Attached Listeners**.
3. <!-- manual: Scroll to the bottom of the panel and click + Attach Listener. The Attach Listener side panel opens with two tabs: -->
4. <!-- manual: Pick the listener to attach. The panel closes and the Attached Listeners list in the left nav now includes both listeners: Click any listener name in this list to edit its configuration inline on the right. -->
